title: Errors and diagnostics
summary: Find an error by its stable ID and follow the remedy for the actual failing component.
html:
Errors and diagnostics

An SMTO error shows a readable ID such as SMTO-LLM-0001. Use Explain this error to open its permanent Manual page, or search the Error Catalog by ID, GUID, slug or older error name. Each page explains what happened, how to diagnose it, what can be fixed, how to verify the change and what to avoid.

The Error ID identifies the kind of failure. The occurrence ID identifies this particular observation. Keep both when reporting a persistent problem, together with safe task and operation references. Technical details may be shortened and private values removed; exact execution receipts remain the source for completed work.

The main error card shows what was observed and the next useful check. When the occurrence retained a safe fact, such as a timeout or token count, the card includes it. A possible cause is a lead to investigate, not a finding. The Manual explains the error type; it cannot know facts that were never recorded for your occurrence.

For example, a 120-second model request timeout means a connection or read wait reached its limit. It does not prove the model crashed or that the whole request lasted exactly 120 seconds. Check provider health first. A suggested longer wait is a diagnostic test, and a changed task setting applies to a new task.

Follow the control named by the error. A model request timeout, a foreground command timeout and a Task Contract output limit belong to different controls. A setting link opens the owning Settings section and focuses a specific control when one is available. Model connection and generation links may open Model routing so you can choose the relevant role. Opening a link does not change a value. When a setting says new task, changing it does not alter the saved value used by Resume.

For context capacity failures, a tool can finish successfully before the next model request exceeds capacity. Keep its result. The runtime compacts eligible history and then proportionally shortens automatic tool previews, preserving recovery actions. If required context still cannot fit, increase available input capacity or reduce required context; request smaller explicit pages when indicated. Settings → Tool result preview controls head and tail characters and applies at the next model call. Increasing maximum completion tokens reserves more output space and leaves less input space. Do not replay completed work to repair a capacity failure.

A lost connection or missing acknowledgement can leave a mutation's outcome unknown. Inspect the authoritative remote state and the retained receipts before repeating the operation. The diagnostic itself does not authorize retry, acceptance of a changed host identity or weaker permissions.

For an HTTP 403, check the account, resource access and service policy before changing credentials. The status proves that access was denied; it does not by itself identify an expired password or a disabled response format.

If withdrawing a steering instruction is unconfirmed, check that instruction's saved status before sending a replacement. An instruction already claimed or applied cannot be withdrawn by repeating Cancel.

If the Gateway becomes reachable again, check the original operation or job receipt too: a restored connection does not settle what the earlier work did. If a download wait expires, inspect that download's existing status and artifact before clicking Download again. It may still be running or may already have finished.

Every error includes simple steps explaining what to do, why it helps, what success looks like, and what to do if it still fails. Open Show steps on a compact error card for the full explanation. Technical details contains the instructions and diagnostic information for someone maintaining the installation.

Use Copy error details to keep the error reference for the person helping you. This copies the error name and references, not your task content or technical logs. If your browser blocks automatic copying, select and copy the text shown instead. If you manage the installation yourself, Explain this error opens its troubleshooting page.

Some errors have no confirmed quick fix. Their steps explain how to check what happened and get help. If an action may already have happened, check its result before trying it again. A restart or a wait is recommended only when the particular problem supports it. Retired Error IDs remain searchable so historical traces keep their meaning.

Using the diagnostic Console

Open Console from the Agent UI, then follow its sidecar link. The separate listener normally uses port 8015 and the installation login. It can continue showing process measurements when the main UI is slow. Refresh reads cached observations; the page also polls every second.

Read heartbeat ages and sample progress alongside the status label. Connected means a main heartbeat arrived at least once; it does not establish current freshness. A blocked-loop finding compares the thread and event-loop heartbeats. Request/stage entries and bottleneck suggestions are clues to investigate, not execution receipts or proof of a root cause. A missing-process reading can also reflect an inaccessible target, so check the configured PID and permissions.

GPU cards report device-wide readings on the Console host. Busiest-GPU utilization and combined VRAM do not measure the Agent alone or a remote Gateway. -- and chart gaps mean unavailable readings, while 0% is an observed idle value. Missing NVIDIA telemetry does not prevent CPU/process diagnostics.

Capture stacks asks the configured main Agent for a Python thread dump. Use it with the main process that registered the stack handler; a manually chosen PID does not establish that prerequisite. Disabling main console publication also skips automatic handler setup. The result can be captured, unsupported, failed or timed out. It does not cancel or resume task execution. Stack text and prompt previews can contain diagnostic details; review them before sharing a report.

If telemetry is absent, check the target PID, heartbeat publication and matching UDP address/port, then the sidecar sample count. An available page or health route alone does not prove its collector bound successfully. A sidecar restart clears its in-memory observations; the append-only stack file has a separate lifetime.

The Console data and lifecycle diagrams explain these sources, configuration defaults, optional event paths and stack capture.

Retained answers and completion checks

An answer can remain visible while its completion claim is still unverified. Read the accompanying feedback and task status: saved text alone does not prove that the requested action finished. An interrupted response remains incomplete, and changing a completion preference cannot manufacture missing execution evidence.

A current-run completion override can recheck the retained answer without another model call. Other Agent Check recovery actions can re-admit a previously blocked, proved unexecuted operation through normal execution checks. Explicit Pause still holds, and uncertain effects need reconciliation. Global defaults apply to new accepted work; the conversation completion preference also updates eligible queued chat tasks that have never started. Broader scopes do not rewrite an already running task's accepted policy.

The retained-answer and policy flow diagrams explain the two recovery surfaces, stale-decision checks and publication boundaries.

Informational Agent Check observations

Settings → Agent Checks → Monitor disabled Agent Checks shows when a disabled check detects a condition it would normally handle. Fresh installations start with monitoring ON; existing installations retain their setting, and missing legacy values resolve OFF. Changes apply to newly accepted work. Individual switches still control enforcement.

The Activity note says the Agent continued because the check is disabled. Learn more opens the relevant Error Catalog page when the detector has a catalog reference, otherwise the Agent Checks explanation. It is informational, not a failed execution or a request for approval. Monitoring neither blocks the run nor makes additional model calls, and it does not change the truth recorded in execution receipts.

For maintainers, Error identity and diagnostics explains how source causes become public diagnostics, which fields are bounded, and how catalog definitions produce the manual pages. The catalog page describes an error type; an occurrence's retained facts and execution receipts describe what happened in your task.
